name: Body Movement Fluidity
description: Analyzes body movement smoothness to detect synthetic artifacts, anomalies, and characteristic signatures of generative AI models.
algorithm: Body Movement Fluidity — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes body movement naturalness for deepfake detection following Zheng et al. (2021):

1. **Pose Estimation**: Full-body or upper-body pose is estimated per frame using landmark detection (shoulders, elbows, wrists, head, torso). Joint angles and positions are tracked to build temporal motion trajectories for each body part.

2. **Motion Smoothness Analysis**: Natural body movements follow minimum-jerk trajectories (Flash & Hogan, 1985) — meaning the third derivative of position (jerk) is minimized. The method computes jerk profiles for tracked joints. AI-generated body movements may violate this biological constraint, showing either excessive jerk (unnatural abruptness) or unnaturally perfect smoothness (lacking physiological tremor).

3. **Joint Coordination Patterns**: Natural movements exhibit coordinated joint motion governed by biomechanical coupling. The method analyzes inter-joint correlations — shoulder-elbow coordination during gestures, head-torso coupling during turns. Deepfakes may produce joints that move independently in physically impossible ways.

4. **Temporal Frequency Analysis**: Body motion signals are analyzed in frequency domain. Natural movements contain characteristic frequency components: voluntary motion (0-2 Hz), physiological tremor (~8-12 Hz), and postural sway (~0.5 Hz). Generated movements may lack these physiological frequency signatures or produce spectrally flat motion without natural frequency structure.

5. **Fluidity Scoring**: Movement fluidity is quantified by combining jerk metrics, coordination scores, and spectral indicators. Low fluidity scores (jerky, uncoordinated, or spectrally abnormal motion) indicate AI generation. The method is particularly effective for full-body deepfakes where generation artifacts extend beyond the face region.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through body movement fluidity analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
